subject.title: Renderer placeholder leak: `(see attached image)`, `Image reply`, `Audio reply`, `Media reply` leak to human-visible Telegram reply under specific content-classification paths

question: Should Telegram or gateway owners require a current-main outbound payload trace before authorizing a placeholder or reply-media code change?
rationale: The symptom is plausible, but the cited source belongs to distinct prompt and WebChat transcript paths; choosing a repair boundary without the missing Telegram trace risks changing intentional behavior.

options.title: Require instrumented reproduction
options.body: Capture the normalized ReplyPayload and final Telegram Bot API method arguments on current main, then patch the first confirmed display-boundary leak.

options.title: Patch defensively now
options.body: Add Telegram-specific suppression for these exact labels despite lacking evidence that they are the values reaching Telegram.

recommendation.title: Require instrumented reproduction
recommendation.body: Capture the normalized ReplyPayload and final Telegram Bot API method arguments on current main, then patch the first confirmed display-boundary leak.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the cited structured assistant-media/WebChat boundary and can distinguish intentional transcript text from channel-visible content before Telegram owners validate delivery.
